Date January 24, 1939

Subject Articles in Russian newspaper "Novosti Dnia" containing remarks
derogatory to the S.M.Council.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

In connection with the public criticism of the recent decision of the S.M.C. in respect of the exchange adjustments and cost of living bonuses, a series of articles appeared in the local Russian newspaper "Novosti Dnia" edited by Mr. V.A. CHILIKIN. Based mainly on the material published in the Letters to the Editor column of the "North China Daily News", these articles contain several passages, which at the first glance appear to be bad mistranslations. In view, however, of the notoriously slanderous tendencies of the newspaper in question these passages may also be regarded as a deliberate misrepresentation of facts.

A translation of the passages referred to above reads as follows:-

" The saddest thing about it is that it is not the lower ranks who have received the increase. This one could understand, as they also feel the hardships of high cost of living. NO, IT IS TO THE ALREADY SUFFICIENTLY ENRICHED ONES THAT THE INCREASE HAS BEEN GIVEN, WHO IN THE MAJORITY OF CASES ARE THE PROPRIETORS OF FIRMS BRINGING LARGE PROFITS".....

("Nov. Dnia", 16-1-39).

" .. Some writers point out that this fact becomes the more crying one because persons who have been granted such big increases, not only draw colossal salaries, but in addition are the proprietors or partners of large commercial firms"...

( "Nov. Dnia", 17-1-39.)
Leading article.

" The 'Broadminded' writes in the "North China Daily News" that the granting of increase to higher employees undoubtedly constituted a form of dilapidation x) on the part of the S.M.C..."

".. He points out that in connection with the protest against the municipal dilapidation he suggests that etc. "...

( "Nov.Dnia, 23-1-39)

主题 俄文报纸《俄罗斯日报》（Novosti Dnia）上刊登的含有诋毁工部局言论的文章。

由 D.S.I. Prokofiev 撰写。由督察 C. Crawford 转呈。

鉴于公众对工部局近期关于汇率调整和生活费津贴决定的批评，由 V.A. CHILIKIN 先生编辑的本地俄文报纸《俄罗斯日报》刊登了一系列文章。这些文章主要基于《字林西报》“读者来信”栏目发表的材料，其中包含若干段落，初看似乎是拙劣的误译。然而，鉴于该报众所周知的诽谤倾向，这些段落也可被视为故意歪曲事实。

上述段落的译文如下：-

“其中最令人悲哀的是，获得加薪的并非下层职员。如果是他们，人们尚可理解，因为他们也感受到高昂生活成本带来的艰难。不，加薪给了那些已经足够富有的人，他们在大多数情况下是拥有带来巨额利润公司的业主”……

（《俄罗斯日报》，1939 年 1 月 16 日）。

“……一些作者指出，这一事实之所以更加令人愤慨，是因为获得如此大幅加薪的人，不仅领取巨额薪水，而且还是大型商业公司的业主或合伙人”……

（《俄罗斯日报》，1939 年 1 月 17 日。）
社论。

“‘Broadminded’在《字林西报》上写道，给高级雇员加薪无疑构成了工部局的一种挥霍 x) ……”

“……他指出，针对市政挥霍提出的抗议，他建议等等……”

（《俄罗斯日报》，1939 年 1 月 23 日）

Налогоплательщики возмущены
что муниципалитет за их счет щедро вознаграждает
себя самого.

Муниципальные главари получили колоссальную прибавку к своим и без того громадным окладам.
Но за то низших служащих обошли; на них сделали „Экономию".

Поток писем и протестов во все редакции иностранных газет говорит о том справедливом возмущении резидентов международного сеттльмента.

Вопрос о двойном увеличении жалованья некоторым высшим служащим шанхайского Муниципального Совета вызвал в городе самые разнообразные отклики, о чем свидетельствует ряд писем в иностранных газетах.

В одном из писем автор его пишет
„Когда большую фирму или большую семью постигает несчастье, то слуг обычно не просят страдать вместе с хозяевами. Если же слуги согласны страдать вместе, то они уже больше не слуги, а друзья. Служащие муниципалитета не сделали этого благородного жеста.

Они забыли свои преимущества и выгоды, которые они в течение многих лет имели от Ш.М.С. и ведут себя, как слуги. Сегодня, когда Шанхай борется за свою жизнь, и частные коммерсанты и их служащие не знают до каких пределов может дойти сокращение жалованья и заработка, эти муниципальные слуги получают надбавку на две трети и даже на три трети жалованья.

Самое печальное, что надбавили не низшим служащим. Это было бы понятно, так как они тоже чувствуют себя стесненно из-за дороговизны. Нет, прибавку получили люди, уже достаточно обогащенные, в большинстве служащие у ющие собственными фирмами, приносящими им крупные доходы. Почему это произошло? Разве они — олимпийцы, на которых мы смертные можем смотреть только снизу? Нам объяснили, что эти люди, услугами которых пользуется Ш. М. С. отличаются такими способностями и знаниями, что они могли бы заработать больше, чем в муниципалитете. Я с этим совершенно не согласен.

Во-первых, для Шанхая не обязательно нанимать людей обязательно нанимать людей такого широкого размаха. В конце концов, международный сеттльмент по величине не больше любого небольшого города. Во вторых, мы знаем лично некоторых из этих людей. Известно, что они обогатились исключительно от Ш.М.С., и теперь им, конечно, не трудно расстаться с Шанхаем. В третьих, когда они поступили на службу в Ш.М.С. они довольствовались сначала скромным жалованьем. Я думаю, что сеттльмент выдержит эту лишнюю обузу, но прибавка остается, все-таки, совершенно немотивированной и неоправданной. Будем надеяться, что счастливы хотя бы порадуют благотворительным обществам города длинными чеками. В другом письме его автор пишет, что муниципалитет бывал уже мишенью нападений, тем не менее, он не считается ни с чем, и за одной ошибкой совершает другую. Ш.М.С. становится автократическим учреждением. Конечно, налогоплательщики могут собраться и изменить это положение. Они должны контролировать дела Ш.М.С. и не разрешать немногим делать все, что им захочется. Мой протест останется гласом вопиющего в пустыне. Мне кажется, что письмо мое не принесет никакой пользы, но может быть я ошибаюсь. Автор третьего письма пишет, что Ш. М. С. время от времени чересчур щедро распоряжается деньгами налогоплательщиков. Не считаясь с теперешними политическими и экономическими условиями Ш. М. С. назначает жалованья на тысячи долларов в месяц, хотя для муниципальной работы в Шанхае не требуются такие люди, как Геддес или Неффилд. Я считаю, что если эти люди не согласны работать за нормальное вознаграждение, они должны быть сняты, и я уверен, что от этой перемены город ничего не потеряет. Хорошо бы если бы ассоциация английских резидентов созвала собрание и обсудила этот вопрос. Следующее письмо называется „Несчастные налогоплательщики", подписанное — „Изумленный". „Изумленный" поражается, почему низшие служащие получили надбавку на дороговизну только в размере 15 процентов их жалованья, а люди, уже получающие грандиозное жалованье, получили надбавку чуть ли не в 100 процентов. „Я чувствую отвращение, — пишет он, — от такого положения вещей, и надеюсь, что будет положен конец этой бессмысленной расточительности". „Разгневанный налогоплательщик" пишет, что при такой надбавке один человек на высоком посту будет обходится Ш.М.С. более 6.000 долларов в месяц, и настаивает на немедленном созыве собрания налогоплательщиков. В ироническом оттенке написано письмо подписанное „американский критик". Автор его удивляется, что в городе где за первый год военных событий умерло 50.000 китайских детей в беженских лагерях, возможны такие вещи. „Я настолько возмущен, — пишет он, — этой жалостью к богатым англичанам, что буду рад, если китайцы окончательно, совершенно изгонят этих англичан из Китая".

1939 年 1 月 16 日

纳税人感到愤怒，
因为市政当局以他们的钱为代价慷慨地
酬劳自己。

市政头目们在其原本就已巨大的薪金基础上获得了巨额的加薪。
但低级职员却被忽略了；在他们身上实现了“节约”。

流向所有外文报纸编辑部的信件和抗议浪潮表明了国际租界居民这种正当的愤怒。

上海工部局给某些高级职员双倍加薪的问题在市内引起了各种各样的反响，外文报纸上的一系列信件证明了这一点。

在其中一封信中，作者写道：
“当一家大公司或一个大家庭遭遇不幸时，通常不会要求仆人与主人一起受苦。如果仆人同意一起受苦，那么他们就不再是仆人，而是朋友。市政职员并没有做出这种高尚的姿态。

他们忘记了多年来从上海工部局获得的特权和利益，表现得像仆人一样。今天，当上海为生存而战，私人商人及其雇员不知道薪水和收入会缩减到何种程度时，这些市政仆人却获得了三分之二甚至三分之三的薪金加薪。

最可悲的是，加薪的不是低级职员。这本来是可以理解的，因为他们也因物价昂贵而感到拮据。不，得到加薪的是那些已经足够富有的人，他们大多数是为自己工作的、拥有带来巨大收入公司的业主。为什么会发生这种情况？难道他们是奥林匹斯山上的神祇，我们这些凡人只能仰视吗？有人向我们解释说，这些为上海工部局服务的人具有这样的能力和知识，以至于他们本可以赚取比在市政当局更多的收入。我完全不同意这种说法。

首先，上海并不一定非要雇佣这种规模宏大的人才。毕竟，国际租界的面积并不比任何一个小城市大。其次，我们 personally 认识其中一些人。众所周知，他们完全是依靠上海工部局致富的，现在对他们来说，离开上海当然不难。第三，当他们受雇于上海工部局时，起初满足于微薄的薪水。我认为租界能承受这一额外的负担，但加薪仍然是完全缺乏动机和理由的。让我们希望至少他们会用长长的支票让城市的慈善团体高兴一下。在另一封信中，作者写道，市政当局以前曾是攻击的目标，尽管如此，它不顾一切，犯了一个错误后又犯另一个错误。上海工部局正变成一个专制机构。当然，纳税人可以集会改变这种状况。他们必须控制上海工部局的事务，不允许少数人为所欲为。我的抗议将是荒野中的呼喊。我觉得我的信不会带来任何好处，但也许我错了。第三封信的作者写道，上海工部局时不时地过于慷慨地支配纳税人的钱。上海工部局不考虑当前的政治和经济状况，任命月薪数千美元的人员，尽管在上海的市政工作中并不需要像 Geddes 或 Neffield 这样的人。我认为，如果这些人不同意按正常报酬工作，就应该解雇他们，我相信城市不会因这种变动而遭受任何损失。如果英国居民协会能召集会议讨论这个问题就好了。下一封信题为“不幸的纳税人”，署名为“惊讶者”。“惊讶者”对低级职员仅获得相当于其薪水 15% 的生活费津贴，而那些已经领取巨额薪水的人却获得了几乎 100% 的津贴感到震惊。“我对这种状况感到厌恶，”他写道，“并希望这种无意义的浪费能够终结。”“愤怒的纳税人”写道，按照这种加薪幅度，一名身居高位的人员每月将耗费上海工部局超过 6,000 美元，并坚持立即召开纳税人会议。一封署名为“美国评论家”的信带有讽刺意味。作者惊讶于在一个军事事件第一年就有 50,000 名中国儿童在难民营中死亡的城市里，竟可能发生这样的事情。“我对这种对富裕英国人的怜悯感到如此愤怒，”他写道，“如果中国人最终彻底将这些英国人赶出中国，我会很高兴。”

pages.en:
17-1-39

Шанхай, 17-го января
Лишній козырь.

Очередной злобой дня Шанхая является вопрос о прибавках к жалованью высших муниципальных служащих ШМС. В то время, как рядовые служащие того же муниципалитета получили, в связи с неблагоприятным курсом местного доллара и общей дороговизной жизни, прибавку в пределах 15 процентов, жалованье главных руководителей муниципалитета оказалось увеличенным почти на сто процентов.

Этот факт вызвал серьезныя нареканія со стороны целаго ряда отдельных налогоплательщиков, поспешивших выступить с открытыми письмами на страницах местных газет. Указывая на совершенно неуместную в настоящее время расточительность, некоторые авторы подчеркивают, что факт этот тем более вопиющ, что лица, получившія столь крупныя прибавки, мало того, что получают колоссальные оклады, но еще вдобавок являются владельцами или участниками крупных коммерческих предприятий. Возмущенные авторы писем категорически не согласны с обычно выдвигаемым доводом, согласно которому ответственные руководители ШМС являются настолько незаменимыми, что оплата их труда не может быть нормальна на основании общих принципов. Авторы писем указывают, что Международный Сеттльмент вовсе не имеет необходимости администрироваться какими-нибудь сверх-гениями. По количеству своего населения и по своим размерам, он нисколько не отличается от лю

бого более или менее крупнаго огорода. Что же касается некотораго своеобразия его международно-политической и международно-правовой физиономии, то нельзя забывать, что наиболее деликатные дипломатические вопросы, связанные с Сеттльментом и требующие от его руководителей особой квалификации, разрешаются не столько непосредственными руководителями ШМС, сколько консульским корпусом и соответствующими консульскими властями. Поэтому нет основания к непомерному увеличению расходных статей муниципального бюджета, связанных с дополнительным вознаграждением и без того хорошо обеспеченных людей.

Во всяком случае, было бы куда более справедливым, если бы эти дополнительные суммы были бы распределены между рядовыми служащими муниципалитета, в особенности же между теми категориями служащих, которые, как, например, агенты муниципальной полиции, несут на себе очень тяжелое бремя охраны жизней и имущества граждан в период шанхайских военных событий и продолжают нести его сейчас, в условиях порожденнаго войной бандитизма и преступности.

Возможно не сомневаться, что указанныя прибавки высшим служащим ШМС дадут лишній козырь в руки всем тем элементам, которые хотели бы изменить, как систему выборов, так и персональный состав Совета.
Вл. Стахов.

1939年1月17日

上海，1月17日
额外的王牌。

上海当前的热门话题是工部局（S.M.C.）高级职员加薪的问题。当该市政机构的普通职员因当地美元汇率不利及生活普遍昂贵而获得不超过15%的加薪时，市政机构主要领导的薪水却增加了近百分之百。

这一事实引起了许多个别纳税人的严重非议，他们急忙在当地报纸的版面上发表公开信。一些作者指出，在目前时期这种浪费是完全不合时宜的，并强调，鉴于获得如此巨额加薪的人士不仅领取着庞大的薪金，而且还是大型商业企业的所有者或参与者，这一事实更显得令人愤慨。这些愤怒的信作者坚决反对通常提出的论点，即工部局的高级主管是如此不可或缺，以至于不能根据一般原则来规范他们的薪酬。信的作者们指出，公共租界完全不需要由任何超级天才来管理。就其人口数量和规模而言，它与任何一个较大或较小的菜园并无二致。至于其国际政治和国际法律面貌的某些特殊性，人们不应忘记，与租界有关且要求其领导人具备特殊资格的最微妙的外交问题，与其说是由工部局的直接领导人解决，不如说是由领事团和相应的领事当局解决的。因此，没有理由过度增加市政预算中与额外酬金相关的支出项目，而这些酬金是支付给那些已经待遇优厚的人们的。

无论如何，如果将这些额外款项分配给市政机构的普通职员，特别是那些在上海市军事事件期间承担着保卫公民生命和财产重任，并在目前战争引发的匪患和犯罪条件下继续承担这一重担的职员类别（例如巡捕房警员），那将会公平得多。

毫无疑问，给予工部局高级职员的上述加薪，将为所有那些希望改变选举制度以及工部局董事会人员构成的势力提供额外的王牌。
弗·斯塔霍夫（Vl. Stakhov）。

NOVOSTI DNIA, January 23, 1939

Горячка поnemuго
проходит.

Тон писем, протестующих против действий Ш. М. С. начинает спадать.

Муниципальный скандал в связи с непропорціональным увеличением жалованья высшим служащим ШМС явился как бы толчком к дальнѣйшему вскрытію и разоблаченію всѣх ненормальностей, существующих въ Шанхаѣ и особенно углубившихся со времени военныхъ событій.

Читатели продолжаютъ бомбардировать редакціи всѣхъ газет письмами, освѣщая наболевшіе вопросы съ той, то съ другой стороны.

"Широко-мыслящій" пишетъ въ "Н.Ч.Д.Н.", — что увеличеніе жалованья высшимъ служащимъ было несомнѣнно формой хищенія со стороны ШМС но онъ оправдываетъ высшихъ служащихъ тѣмъ, что они приняли грандіозную прибавку, будучи только людьми!!!

"Р.Ж.Б." приводитъ примѣръ въ той фирмѣ, гдѣ онъ служитъ. — Тамъ были увеличены въ первую голову жалованья мало получающимъ служащимъ. Такъ, напримѣръ, служащіе съ жалованьемъ въ 50 дол. получили прибавку въ 100 процентовъ, а служащіе же съ жалованьемъ въ 1.000 долл. не получили ничего.

Въ заключеніе онъ говоритъ, что интересно бы сравнить жалованья служащихъ французскаго муниципалитета съ жалованьями служащихъ ШМС.

Въ связи съ назначеніемъ особаго комитета для разслѣдованія спора, "Глочестеръ" находитъ, что во всякомъ спорѣ должны принимать участіе обѣ спорящія стороны.

Поэтому онъ считаетъ, что, несмотря на назначеніе комитета, необходимо въ общемъ собраніи налогоплательщиковъ не отпадать.

Дама, письмо которой мы на-дняхъ помѣщали подъ псевдонимомъ "Поневоли похулишь", снова пишетъ длинное письмо, въ которомъ привѣтствуетъ предложеніе о сидячей забастовкѣ.

Она служитъ въ ШМС и по ея словамъ, готова принять участіе въ забастовкѣ, если ее поддержатъ нѣсколько изъ ея коллегъ. Но она смотритъ на забастовку и на организацію трэд-юніоновъ пессимистически, считая большинство людей безхребетными, способными только сидѣть и стонать, вмѣстѣ того, чтобы взять быка за рога.

Въ заключеніе она, все-таки выражаетъ надежду, что налогоплательщики общими усиліями сумѣютъ отобрать астрономическія жалованья у муниципальныхъ тузовъ.

Послѣдній корреспондентъ подписывается "Не желающій, чтобы ему садились на голову".

Онъ указываетъ, что въ связи съ протестомъ противъ муниципальнаго хищенія, онъ предлагаетъ также протестовать противъ спекуляціи квартирохозяевъ и даже поставить этотъ вопросъ передъ ШМС.

Онъ считаетъ, что налогоплательщики должны отказаться платить налоги, ренту и сверхъ-налоги до тѣхъ поръ, пока они не будутъ снижены. Если бы президенты Сеттльмента поступили такимъ образомъ, Совѣту пришлось бы подумать о томъ, какъ снизить налоги.

《今日新闻》（NOVOSTI DNIA），1939年1月23日

被迫发牢骚的热潮
正在消退。

抗议工部局（S.M.C.）行为的信件语调开始减弱。

与工部局高级职员薪水不成比例的增加有关的市政丑闻，仿佛成为了进一步揭露和曝光上海存在的所有不正常现象的推动力，这些现象自军事事件以来尤为加剧。

读者们继续用信件轰炸各家报社的编辑部，从不同角度阐述令人痛心的问题。

一位署名“思想开阔者”的人在《N.Ch.D.N.》报上写道——给高级职员加薪无疑是工部局的一种盗窃形式，但他为高级职员辩护说，他们接受巨大的加薪只是因为他们是人！！！

“R.Zh.B.”举了他所任职公司的例子。——在那里，首先增加的是低薪职员的薪水。例如，月薪50美元的职员获得了100%的加薪，而月薪1,000美元的职员则什么也没得到。

最后他说，将法租界公董局职员的薪水与工部局职员的薪水进行比较将是很有趣的。

鉴于已任命一个特别委员会来调查这一争端，“格洛斯特”（Glochester）认为，在任何争端中，争议双方都应参与。

因此，他认为，尽管已任命了委员会，但在纳税人大会上仍不应缺席。

前几天我们以笔名“被迫发牢骚”刊登了其信件的一位女士，再次写了一封长信，她在信中欢迎静坐罢工的提议。

她在工部局任职，据她说，如果有几位同事支持她，她准备参加罢工。但她对罢工和工会组织持悲观态度，认为大多数人没有骨气，只会坐着呻吟，而不是去直面困难（抓住公牛的角）。

最后，她仍然表示希望，纳税人通过共同努力，能够从市政大亨手中夺回那些天文数字般的薪水。

最后一位通讯员署名为“不愿被人骑在头上”。

他指出，鉴于对市政盗窃行为的抗议，他建议也抗议房东的投机行为，甚至将这个问题提交给工部局。

他认为，纳税人应拒绝缴纳税款、租金和附加税，直到这些费用降低为止。如果租界的各位总裁（presidents）采取这种做法，董事会将被迫考虑如何降低税收。

pages.en:
S.M.C. Increase:
The Servant's Due
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—When a great firm or a great family falls on evil days the servants cannot be asked to suffer with them. If they offer to do so they become no longer servants but friends. Our servants, the employees of the Shanghai Municipal Council, have not made the latter gallant gesture. With many years of benefits forgot, they have chosen to remain servants and to demand the servants' due.
At a time when Shanghai's is battling for its life, when the private business man and his employees are wondering in what direction they can next cut down and economize in order to be able to live at all, these municipal servants of ours have had their pay increased by two-thirds and "three-thirds"—one might exaggerate a bit and say doubled.
It is not the lower ranks to whom this amazing thing has happened. We might have envied them their luck—but at least we should have realized that they, with us, were feeling the pinch. "To him that hath shall be given"—and it is to the already richly remunerated men in the high ranks of S.M.C. employment that this doubling of pay has been vouchsafed. At no time can H.C.L. have been to these men anything more vital than an annoying curtailment of money to burn.
From what quarter did the incitement to this amazing use of public money come? Our Municipal Council is composed of men? heads of rich firms or in the safe shelter of huge corporations able to give them allowances of such description that they are sheltered from the winds of adversity. Can it be that they have forgotten or never experienced how these winds can blow? Is it possible that to them the case of these highly-paid municipal employees really does seem a hard one? If so, then are they Olympians indeed to whom we poor mortals may look for understanding in vain.
We have been told until we are tired of hearing it that the men engaged by the S.M.C. are of such ability that in private practice they could earn more than they are being paid by Shanghai. I take this opportunity of saying that I, for one, do not accept this statement.
In the first place, Shanghai does not require employees of such calibre. It would be an extravagance to engage such men. The scope of the International Settlement is exceedingly limited—it is indeed, only a big town.
In the second place, we know the origin of some of the men who are now occupying high positions. No offence is meant to them when we say that if we were in the monetary position which they have attained to through entering our Municipal employ we should be very glad quietly to call ourselves and Shanghai quits as far as mutual obligation was concerned and should not thank anybody who made a song about it.
In the third place, when these men accepted service in the Shanghai municipality, were they not well content to take their dollar salary? The good years have so far incomparably outweighed the bad. The lists were already closing down over the future when certain of those who are now most richly to profit by the new salary increases first threw in their fortunes with Shanghai. If their augmen was not sufficient to visualize the possibility of what has now happened to the dollar, they cannot be such invaluable acquisitions. The least among business men would have been wiser.
Fourthly and lastly, men who enter a service deliberately choose the peace of mind provided by regular pay and a pension. It comes in place of the possibility of much higher returns only to be won by unremitting effort in open competition. Even with a depreciated dollar, our Municipal

service is still a fine one.
I suppose that the Settlement can manage to repay this new burden laid upon it. What is much harder to support is the parallel to character. There is no magic place from which comes the money to make the servants richer. It is extracted from the pockets of the small man as well as from the coffers of the big corporations. It will soon be a case of "Cut down the coal bill. Mother—expenses are rising again." And when wages day comes round and increases are pouched in Administration Building, let us hope the various charitable societies will be kept busy acknowledging cheques from happy S.M.C. employees.
PLAY THE GAME.
Shanghai, Jan. 18.

Can Anything Be Done?
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I raise my hat to you for your leader of this morning regarding the S.M.C. increases and heartily agree with all what you say, but I wonder if it will do any good.
The S.M.C. have been the target of many attacks, but they appear to be immune of feelings for no sooner are they criticized than they commit another, shall we say, as you say, blunder; or is it a defiance?
It has always appeared to me how helpless the ratepayers are and how little they are allowed to say in the management of their money.
The S.M.C. is autocratic and although you are influential, your influence in this respect is of no avail. Surely the ratepayers can gather together and correct the present system. They should control S.M.C. affairs and not allow the few that are in power to do as they please.
Our protest may be a voice in the wilderness, but we are in an era where that can be remedied. We can use a microphone with a very, very loud speaker, so to speak.
I end my letter still thinking it will not do any good, but may be I am wrong.
WATTS D. USE.
Shanghai, Jan. 14.

Undue Generosity
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—During my many years' residence in the International Settlement of Shanghai, successive municipal councils have done many strange and unaccountable things and have at times been unduly generous with the Ratepayers' money.
But the sheer ineptitude and crass ignorance of the surrounding political conditions, their present action in increasing by apparently thousands of dollars a month the salaries of the Heads of municipal departments surely transcends all the previous actions of their predecessors.
There being only about eight square miles of territory to control, it is difficult to believe that men of such outstanding ability as a Goddes or a Nutfield are required for these municipal jobs, but even if such are required, it is quite clear that local harassed merchants are not prepared to pay these high salaries under present uncertain conditions.
It would therefore appear that if the present incumbents of these posts are not prepared to work for a reasonable salary they should be replaced by men of lesser qualifications but of greater basic experience, and I for one find it difficult to believe that this substitution would be any the worse for the Council.
As the Municipal cannot remember the names of the members of the Committee who recommended these colossal increases, I would be interested to know whether the salaries of the departmental heads in any of the other Treaty Ports have been increased in like manner.
Perhaps the British Residents'

Association could call a members' meeting to discuss the matter before the Ratepayers are finally committed to such a potentially disastrous course of action.
MERCHANT.
Shanghai, Jan. 14.

Unfortunate Ratepayers
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—You are to be congratulated on the exceedingly appropriate and succinct leading article which appeared in to-day's issue of your paper.
Why on earth the smaller paid S.M.C. employees should only get 15 per cent. high cost of living allowance when the men in pivotal positions are now to get anything up to 100 per cent. passes my comprehension. Surely some of the smaller paid employees also have sterling commitments or would have them if they could afford to!
I cannot help feeling disgusted that such an unfair state of affairs should have been permitted to come into force and I sincerely hope that ways and means will be devised to put a stop to such senseless method of dissipating revenue wrested from the unfortunate ratepayer of which I am one.
SURPRISED.
Shanghai, Jan. 14.

Ratepayer's Meeting Wanted
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—The announcement about increase in your paper on Friday was staggering. Your leader on Saturday was excellent and very correctly represented the opinion of everyone except perhaps the recipients of the bonus of 66 per cent. and 100 per cent.
The only question is, what are we to do in order to prevent this injustice and this reckless expenditure of money? We cannot afford such a cultural necessity as the orchestra, and we cannot pay our police enough to retain them, yet one man alone will cost us, everything included, over $6,000—a month. What do we do about it? Can we call a special ratepayers meeting to pass a vote of censure on the Council and if necessary demand the immediate retirement of all heads of departments and the substitution of men who would be willing and anxious to work for a remuneration more in keeping with the times?
No wonder there are revolutions!!
FURIOUS RATEPAYER.
Shanghai, Jan. 14.

A Terrific Blunder
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—With China still out of gear with the rest of the world, and foreigners and Chinese of the Settlement suffering from the effects of currency manipulation and adverse trading conditions, no apology is necessary for emphasizing the profound importance of checking the terrific blunder of the S.M.C., and its Staff Committee on the question of salary increases.
The editorial appearing in today's issue of the "North-China Daily News" is to be commended, and should be sufficient urge for the foreign and Chinese Residents' Associations to take immediate action at such reckless prodigality can only be found in the pages of "Shanghai, the Paradise of Adventurers."
The Municipal Rate up to 16 per cent., motor car licences and other taxes increased 10 per cent., the unwarranted expense of an orchestra, the running of foreign residential areas by borrowing in close proximity to the scene of chaos and
pages.zh:
工部局加薪：
仆役应得之分
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——当一家大公司或大家族遭遇厄运时，不能要求仆人与其共患难。若他们主动提出如此做，便不再是仆人，而是朋友了。我们的仆人，即上海工部局的雇员们，并未做出这般英勇的姿态。他们忘却了多年来的恩惠，选择继续充当仆人的角色，并索要仆役应得之分。

在上海为生存而挣扎之际，当私人商贾及其雇员都在琢磨下一步该从何处削减开支、节约成本以维持生计时，我们这些市政仆役的薪水却增加了三分之二乃至“三分之三”——或许可以稍加夸张地说，翻了一番。

发生这一惊人事件的并非底层职员。我们本可羡慕他们的好运——但至少我们应意识到，他们与我们一样，正感受着经济紧缩的压力。“凡有的，还要加给他”——而这番加薪殊荣，恰恰降临在工部局高层中那些早已薪酬丰厚的人士身上。对于这些人而言，生活成本指数（H.C.L.）的调整从来都不过是令其恼火的、对可供挥霍之钱财的一点削减罢了。

这种令人惊愕的公款使用方式，究竟是受何方鼓动所致？我们的工部局由何人组成？他们是富商巨贾的首脑，或是身处大型企业的庇护之下，享受着足以使其免受逆境风雨侵袭的津贴。难道是他们忘记了，或是从未体验过这些风雨是如何吹打的吗？难道在他们看来，这些高薪市政雇员的处境真的显得艰难吗？若是如此，那他们确是奥林匹斯山上的神祇，而我们这些可怜的凡人只能徒劳地寻求他们的理解。

我们已听得厌倦不堪的说法是，工部局所聘人员才干出众，若在私营机构任职，其收入将高于上海方面支付的薪俸。我借此机会声明，就我个人而言，我不接受这一说法。

首先，上海并不需要如此高素质的雇员。聘用此类人员实属奢侈。公共租界的管辖范围极其有限——它确实只不过是一个大城镇而已。

其次，我们知道目前身居高位者中部分人员的出身。此言绝非冒犯，我们要说的是，倘若我们处于他们通过进入市政部门工作而获得的金钱地位，我们将非常乐意 quietly 自称与上海两清，互不相欠，并且不会感谢任何为此大肆宣扬的人。

第三，当这些人接受上海市政服务时，他们当初不也心满意足地领取着以美元计价的薪水吗？好年景至今为止远远多于坏年景。当某些如今将从新一轮加薪中获利最丰的人最初将其命运与上海绑在一起时，未来的账簿已然合拢。若他们的眼光不足以预见美元如今可能发生的变故，那他们便算不上是无价之宝。即便是最普通的商人也会比他们更明智。

第四且最后，投身于公职的人，是刻意选择了定期薪俸和养老金所带来的心安。这是以放弃在公开竞争中通过不懈努力才可能获得的更高回报为代价的。即便美元贬值，我们的市政

服务依然是一份优差。

我想，租界尚能设法偿还强加于其上的这一新负担。更难承受的是由此引发的品格类比问题。并没有某种魔法之地能变出钱来让仆人们变得更富有。这笔钱既是从小人物的口袋中榨取，也是从大公司的金库中抽取。很快就会出现这样的情况：“缩减煤费账单吧，母亲——开销又涨了。”而当发薪日来临，加薪款项在行政大楼中被装入腰包时，让我们希望各类慈善团体会忙于接收来自快乐的工部局雇员们的支票。

PLAY THE GAME.
上海，1月18日。

还能做些什么吗？
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——我对您今晨关于工部局加薪的社论脱帽致敬，并衷心赞同您所说的一切，但我怀疑这是否会有任何成效。

工部局一直是众多攻击的目标，但他们似乎对情感免疫，因为刚一受到批评，他们就犯下另一个，不妨说，如您所言，愚蠢的错误；或者说，这是一种挑衅？

在我看米，纳税人总是显得无助，且在管理自己的钱财方面几乎没有发言权。

工部局是独裁的，尽管您颇具影响力，但在这方面您的影响力无济于事。纳税人肯定可以聚集起来，纠正目前的体制。他们应当掌控工部局的事务，而不允许少数掌权者随心所欲。

我们的抗议可能是荒野中的呼声，但我们身处一个可以补救这种状况的时代。可以说，我们可以使用带有非常、非常大喇叭的麦克风。

我在结束这封信时仍认为这不会有任何好处，但也可能是我错了。
WATTS D. USE.
上海，1月14日。

过度的慷慨
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——在我居住于上海公共租界的多年间，历届工部局做过许多奇怪且无法解释的事情，有时在花费纳税人的钱财上过度慷慨。

但是，他们对周围政治环境的纯粹无能及粗陋无知，以及他们目前每月将市政各部门主管的薪水增加数千美元之举，无疑超越了其前任的所有既往行为。

管辖区域仅约八平方英里，很难相信需要像 Goddes 或 Nutfield 这样能力杰出的人才来担任这些市政职务，但即便确实需要此类人才，也很明显，在当前不确定的局势下，当地备受困扰的商人们并不准备支付如此高昂的薪水。

因此，如果目前担任这些职位的人不愿意以合理的薪水工作，那么他们应由资历较浅但具备更多基础经验的人取代，就我个人而言，很难相信这种替换会对工部局造成任何不利影响。

既然工部局记不住推荐这些巨额加薪的委员会成员的名字，我倒很有兴趣知道，其他任何通商口岸的部门主管薪水是否也以类似方式增加了。

也许英国居民协会可以在纳税人最终陷入这一潜在灾难性行动之前，召集一次会员会议来讨论此事。
MERCHANT.
上海，1月14日。

不幸的纳税人
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——贵报今日刊登的那篇极其恰当且简练的社论值得祝贺。

为何薪水较低的工部局雇员仅获得15%的高生活费津贴，而关键岗位的人员现在却能获得高达100%的津贴，这令我无法理解。肯定有些薪水较低的雇员也有英镑计价的债务负担，或者如果他们负担得起的话，也会有！

我不禁感到厌恶，竟然允许如此不公平的状态生效，我真诚希望能想出办法，制止这种毫无意义地挥霍从不幸纳税人（我也是其中之一）手中夺来的收入的做法。
SURPRISED.
上海，1月14日。

要求召开纳税人会议
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——周五贵报上关于加薪的公告令人震惊。周六的社论非常出色，非常准确地代表了除那些获得66%和100%奖金的受益者之外每个人的意见。

唯一的问题是，为了防止这种不公和鲁莽的金钱挥霍，我们该怎么做？我们负担不起像管弦乐队这样的文化必需品，我们也无法支付足够的薪水来留住警察，然而仅一个人每月就要花费我们超过6,000美元——包含所有费用。我们该怎么办？我们能否召开特别纳税人会议，通过对工部局的谴责决议，并在必要时要求所有部门主管立即离职，并由那些愿意且渴望以更符合时代水平的报酬工作的人取而代之？

难怪会发生革命！！
FURIOUS RATEPAYER.
上海，1月14日。

巨大的失误
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——鉴于中国仍与世界其他地区脱节，且租界内的外侨和华人正遭受货币操纵和不利的贸易条件的影响，强调制止工部局及其人事委员会在加薪问题上的巨大失误具有深远的重要性，此举无需道歉。

今日《字林西报》刊登的社论值得称赞，这应足以促使外籍和华人居民协会立即采取行动，因为这种鲁莽的挥霍无度只会在《上海：冒险家的乐园》的书页中找到。

市政捐税上调至16%，汽车牌照及其他税费增加10%，管弦乐队的不合理开支，通过在混乱现场附近借款来运营外籍人士居住区，以及

令人反感的工厂，可怕的广告牌，以及最近在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）上搭建的一群几乎不比泥棚好多少的建筑等等，等等，这些都是现任工部局在那些“受过训练、经验丰富且能力一流”的人士协助下所批准授权的充分例证。

pages.en:
S.M.C. Increases:
Another Point of View

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—I have read with interest the various letters published regarding the recent increase in wages given by the Municipal Council. When one views the situation in the proper light one must honestly admit that the Council has blundered, in the way the increases have been proportioned. One cannot condemn the officials of the Council for accepting the increase, it is only human nature that everyone will take all they can get with open arms. The main fault appears to lie in the way the increase has been proportioned; instead of the lower ratings getting the lion's share they have been allotted the smallest, and the officials receiving the largest salary receive the largest increase. The whole thing is absolutely absurd, and I wonder how the Accountant Officer of the Council arrived at such a step.

I maintain that technical men recruited from home should be paid a good and reasonable salary and so should be fully compensated for their loss due to the drop in the local dollar; one cannot expect a technical man to come out from England and receive less salary than he can command at home, and I for one support that point. I myself hold an appointment similar to an official in the Council regarding my own profession and I was brought out from England. I have exactly the same type of duty to perform as the official in the Council, but with not such a large staff, therefore my responsibilities must be more as I do not have the officers and men to assist me. But I am not drawing the salary similar to the Council's official, far from it, my salary would be about a third of it. Although I have had an increase in salary myself and also a small increase to compensate me for the drop in the dollar, I am still worse off financially than when I came to China a few years back, and when my salary is converted into sterling I am drawing the salary I was drawing eight years and more ago.

But the Council's official is not in the position that I am. When a person is brought out from England he expects to receive a good and reasonable salary to compensate him for coming East; he forsakes advancement and good openings in England and there is no doubt his main intention and idea is to come East and to be able to save sufficient in a reasonable number of years to enable him to go back and retire in comfortable surroundings. These cases must be based on their merits, and I say that if the Council has blundered you cannot blame their servants for accepting the increase. Unfortunately the Council does not appear to take the proper view of the situation; there are no doubt a number of officials termed technical men regarding their profession in the service of the Council, but are that in name only, an official cannot be an expert in more than one thing. If there is a surplus in the Council's purse which they wish to dispose of, let it be distributed in a fair and just manner, so that there will be no cause for complaint. Technical men brought out from home should be compensated for their loss, and the lower ratings and poorer paid Staff given a good and substantial increase to enable them to live like decent citizens and enjoy the proper things in life, then no one will have cause to complain.

I am fighting no one's battle in the affair but just give my view of the situation for what it is worth. It is to be hoped that the Council will see that the wrong is put right as early as possible and assist to maintain a competent and contented body of men in their employ. After all, the Council has some good and competent officials in their employ and probably some not so good.

BROADMINDED.
Shanghai, Jan. 21.
pages.zh:
工部局加薪：
另一种观点

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——我饶有兴致地阅读了近期发表的关于工部局最近增加工资的各种信件。当人们以恰当的眼光审视局势时，必须诚然承认，工部局在分配加薪比例的方式上犯了错误。人们不能谴责接受加薪的工部局官员，因为人人都会张开双臂接纳他们所能得到的一切，这只是人之常情。主要的过错似乎在于加薪的分配方式；低级职员本应获得最大份额，却只分得最少，而薪水最高的官员却获得了最大的增幅。整件事简直荒谬至极，我不知工部局的会计官是如何做出如此决定的。

我认为，从本国招募的技术人员应当获得优厚且合理的薪水，并应就因本地货币贬值所造成的损失给予充分补偿；不能指望一名技术人员从英国来到此地，所得薪水却低于他在本国能获得的水平，我个人支持这一观点。我自己担任的职务与工部局中与其专业相关的官员类似，我也是从英国被聘来的。我所履行的职责与工部局官员完全相同，只是下属人员较少，因此我的责任必然更重，因为我缺乏警官和警员协助。然而，我的薪水并不像工部局官员那样高，远非如此，我的薪水大约只有他们的三分之一。虽然我自己也加了薪，并且为了补偿货币贬值还略有增加，但在经济状况上，我仍不如几年前刚来中国时宽裕，而且当把我的薪水换算成英镑时，我目前的收入水平相当于八年多以前的水平。

但工部局的官员所处的境况与我不同。当一个人从英国被聘来时，他期望获得优厚且合理的薪水，以补偿他东来之举；他放弃了在英国的晋升机会和良好的发展前景，毫无疑问，他的主要意图和想法是来到东方，并在合理的年限内积攒足够的钱财，以便回国后在舒适的环境中退休。这些情况必须根据其本身的是非曲直来评判，我要说的是，如果工部局犯了错误，你不能责怪其雇员接受加薪。不幸的是，工部局似乎未能正确看待局势；无疑有许多在工部局服务的官员在其职业上被称为技术人员，但这只是徒有虚名，一名官员不可能精通不止一件事。如果工部局库中有盈余希望处置，那就应以公平公正的方式进行分配，这样就无人会有怨言。从本国聘来的技术人员应就其损失获得补偿，而低级职员和薪资较低的员工应获得良好且实质性的加薪，使他们能够像体面的公民一样生活，享受生活中应有的事物，这样就无人会有怨言。

在此事中，我并不为任何人争辩，只是提出我对局势的看法，供参考。希望工部局能尽早纠正错误，并协助维持一支能干且满意的雇员队伍。毕竟，工部局雇佣了一些优秀且能干的官员，可能也有一些不那么优秀的。

BROADMINDED.
上海，1月21日。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
（印：File No. ...Y）
No. S. B. 4665.
Special Branch Sydney
Date March 2 1939.

Subject Satirical verses in the evening edition of the "Novosti Dnia"
containing insulting remarks regarding Hitler.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross

In accordance with the instructions of the
D.C. (Special Branch), Messrs. V.A. Chilikin and A.I. Veiss,
publisher and editor respectively of the "Novosti Dnia"
(evening edition), were interviewed at headquarters on
March 1. They were told that the Police strongly objected
to the generally insulting character of the verses accompanying
various anti-German Nazi cartoons which appeared in their
newspaper daily since February 20. It was pointed out to
Mr. Chilikin that the general trend of these cartoons and
especially the verses was not in keeping with the written
undertaking he gave to the Commissioner of Police on September
25, 1937, when the ban on his newspaper was lifted, namely
that he would "refrain from publishing objectionable or abusive
matter of any kind".

In reply Mr. Chilikin raised the point of alleged
discrimination on the part of the police in favour of other
local newspapers such as the "North China Daily News", "China
Press" and "Evening Post & Mercury" in which he claimed
objectionable cartoons appeared from time to time. However,
he admitted that he had been wrong in having published verses
of an insulting character and promised to refrain from printing
matter of this nature in his newspaper in future.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 2.3.39）

FILE
（签名）
C. D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
报告
（印：档案号 ...Y）
编号 S. B. 4665。
特科 悉尼
日期 1939年3月2日。

主题 《每日新闻》晚报版中包含侮辱希特勒言论的讽刺诗。

由 C.D.I. Ross 制作并提交

遵照特科副总监的指示，于3月1日在总部约谈了《每日新闻》（晚报版）的出版人 V.A. Chilikin 先生和编辑 A.I. Veiss 先生。警方告知他们，强烈反对自2月20日起在该报每日刊登的各种反德国纳粹漫画所附带的诗歌中普遍存在的侮辱性质。向 Chilikin 先生指出，这些漫画尤其是所附诗歌的总体倾向，不符合他在1937年9月25日解除对该报禁令时向警务处长作出的书面承诺，即他将“避免刊登任何令人反感或辱骂性的内容”。

作为回应，Chilikin 先生提出了警方涉嫌歧视的问题，称警方偏袒其他本地报纸，如《字林西报》、《大美晚报》和《晚邮报与水星报》，他声称这些报纸不时也会出现令人反感的漫画。然而，他承认刊登具有侮辱性质的诗歌是错误的，并承诺今后不在其报纸上刊登此类内容。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特科 1939年3月2日）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. ... RY No. S. B. D. 1165 Branch ... Date February 28, 1939）

Subject Humorous verses in the "Novosti Dnia" of 27-2-39 (evening edition)
containing an insulting remark regarding Hitler.
Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by G. Gous... S. O.

In every issue of the NOVOSTI DNIA's evening
edition, which made its first appearance on February 20,
1939, appears on the front page a cartoon accompanied by
verses explaining its meaning. The cartoons are invari-
ably of an anti-Nazi character and, as will be observed
from the attached specimens, do not present anything of
an unusual nature. In the verses, however, a tendency
towards insult is clearly noticeable. For instance, ver-
ses accompanying the cartoon in the issue dated 27-2-39,
representing Chamberlain as a Romeo and Hitler - as a
Julia, contain the following passage:-

.."And, lo! There she comes with roses,
Assuming captivating poses..
(Oh, is not she a rot?! )...."

In the Russian language the word translated
as "rot" has several shades of meaning and, if applied to
a human being, has a definitely insulting and offensive
character.

It will be recalled that in connection with cer-
tain articles of an offensive for local Germans character,
the editor of the NOVOSTI DNIA was warned by D.C. (Special
Branch) on 25-11-36, 6-1-37 and 13-1-37 to refrain from
publishing anything likely to offend national feelings of
any section of the foreign community in Shanghai. The
first warning was made at an unofficial request from the
local German Consulate-General.

（批：J.B. P.A. to D.C. (Sp Br) 28/2）

G. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 档案号 ... RY 编号 S. B. D. 1165 股 ... 日期 1939年2月28日）

主题 1939年2月27日《每日新闻》（晚报版）中包含侮辱希特勒言论的幽默诗。
制作人：D.S.I. Prokofiev。提交人：G. Gous... S. O.

在1939年2月20日首次出版的《每日新闻》晚报版的每一期中，头版都刊登一幅漫画，并附有解释其含义的诗句。这些漫画 invariably 具有反纳粹性质，正如从所附样本中所见，并没有呈现任何不寻常的内容。然而，在这些诗句中，明显可以看出一种侮辱的倾向。例如，1939年2月27日那一期中伴随漫画的诗句，将张伯伦描绘为罗密欧，将希特勒描绘为朱丽叶，其中包含以下段落：-

..“看啊！她带着玫瑰走来，
摆出迷人的姿态..
（哦，她难道不是个贱货？！）....”

在俄语中，被翻译为“rot”（贱货/烂人）一词有多种含义层次，如果用于指代人，则具有明确的侮辱性和冒犯性。

回想一下，鉴于某些文章具有冒犯当地德国人的性质，《每日新闻》的编辑曾于1936年11月25日、1937年1月6日和1937年1月13日受到特科副总监的警告，要求避免刊登任何可能冒犯上海外侨社区任何部分民族感情的内容。第一次警告是根据当地德国总领事馆的非正式请求发出的。

（批注：J.B. P.A. 致 特科副总监 2月28日）

G. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

特科副总监。

NOVOSTI DNIA, February 28,1939
(Evening edition)

ДАЕШЬ ДЕТЕЙ!

—Откуда это происходит...
Миг семейной бури...
Де-с ... Девятый вал..
Морщась, смотрит фюрер,
Слушает скандал.

Женушка-негера
Муженька честит:
— Что ты спишь, холера,
Словно рыба—кит?!

Что сказал бы фюрер?!
Ах, лентяй! Ах, спрут!
— Даже ночью, дурень,
Нужен... честный труд!

— Для страны, для "наци"
Дети, ведь, нужны!
Надо постараться
Для своей страны!

MORE CHILDREN!

Knitting his brows, the Fuehrer looks at the scandalous
family scene below.. A violent-tempered wife scolds her
husband...

" Oh,you pest! You sleep like a whale?!

What would the Fuehrer say?!

You sluggard! You poulp!

Even at night honest work is required,you fool!

Don't you know that the country and the "Nazi" want
children!

One must exert one's self for one's own country!

"NOVOSTI DNIA", February 27,1939
(Evening edition)

ПОД БАЛКОНОМ.
(На знаменитый мотив).

И вот вдруг с розами,
Плывя позами,
(Ну, не стервоза ли?!)
Идет... она.
Вай! Вай!

И наш Чемберлен
(Ах, он джентльмен
От самого носа до пяток!),
Любовью сражен,
Красавиц ей
Клянется любить ее свято.

Ах, струны — звонки.
А чувства — тонки...
Пройдем сторонкою,
Оставим их...
Вай! Вай!

Придя под балкон,
"Бей мир бист ду шон"
Стоит Чемберлен напевает.
И струны звенят,
И струны зовут,
Ее на балкон вызывают.

Пройдет много лет,
И новый поэт
Себя обезсмертит в столетьях.
Он чувствами полн,
Напишет роман
О новых Ромео-Джульеттах.

UNDER A BALCONY.

阳台下。
（配著名曲调）。

突然，她带着玫瑰，
摇曳着身姿，
（哼，难道不是个泼妇？！）
走来了……她。
哇！哇！

还有我们的张伯伦
（啊，他是个绅士
从鼻尖到脚后跟都是！），
被爱情击中，
向这位美女
发誓神圣地爱她。

啊，琴弦——清脆。
情感——细腻……
让我们从旁边走过，
让他们去吧……
哇！哇！

来到阳台下，
“你是我的美人”
张伯伦站着吟唱。
琴弦鸣响，
琴弦呼唤，
将她召至阳台。

许多年将过去，
一位新的诗人
将在世纪中使自己不朽。
他充满情感，
将写出一部小说
关于新的罗密欧与朱丽叶。

САМСОНІАДА

Поднимайте выше знамя!
Пусть раздается их звон!
Появился в мірѣ нашемъ
Новоявленный Самсонъ.

Опустилъ свои онъ плечи
(Вся сила — въ волосахъ)
И трепещутъ враги наши,
Притаившись въ кустахъ.

Похваляется Самсонъ:
— Я де, братцы, всѣхъ сильнѣй!
— Я такой красавецъ!
— Что изъ рюмки тянетъ!

И за сѣдло ухватился...
Онъ упалъ, силы нѣтъ...
Нѣтъ, самсонъ не выдержалъ,
Расшибся объ паркетъ!

Очи кровью залиты,
Грудь пылитъ, какъ порохъ...
Призывалъ людей на помощь,
Но... помочь ему не могъ!

Шамар.

SAMSONIADA

参孙记

高举旗帜！
让它们的钟声响起！
在我们的世界里
出现了一位新参孙。

他垂下了肩膀
（力量全在头发里）
我们的敌人颤抖着，
躲在灌木丛中。

参孙夸耀道：
“兄弟们，我比所有人都强！
“我是个美男子！
“从小酒杯里喝酒！”

他抓住了马鞍……
他摔倒了，没力气了……
不，参孙没能撑住，
摔在地板上粉身碎骨！

双眼充血，
胸膛如火药般扬起灰尘……
他呼救人们帮忙，
但是……没人能帮他！

Shamar.

No. S. E. D. 4665
Date 28 11 38

NIPPO
18-11-38

ANTI-JAPANESE BROADCASTING BY RUSSIAN NEWSPAPER

A Russian language daily paper
known as the "Novosti Dnia" located on Avenue Foch and
which is managed by a Russian named Chilikin is notoriously
anti-Japanese. On October 24 the paper established a
radio news section with B. B. Drozdoff as manager. Since
then the section has been broadcasting pro-Chiang Kai Shek
and anti-Japanese news twice every day through the Hwamei
Radio Station(X.M.H.A.) on Race Course Road. The broadcast
is giving rise to much indignation among Japanese residents.
A large part of the news is supplied by the Tass News
agency of Soviet Russia.

The paper in question is undoubtedly
receiving money from the Soviet Government and is working
in accordance with its instructions.
The Japanese censorship authorities
have begun to pay attention to the paper and may suppress
it if necessary.

S.I.
82

俄文报纸的反日广播

一份名为《今日新闻》（Novosti Dnia）的俄文日报，位于福煦路（Avenue Foch），由一名名叫奇利金（Chilikin）的俄国人管理，以强烈的反日立场而臭名昭著。10月24日，该报设立了无线电新闻部，由 B. B. Drozdoff 担任经理。此后，该部门每天两次通过跑马厅路（Race Course Road）的华美电台（X.M.H.A.）广播亲蒋介石和反日的新闻。这些广播引起了日本居民的极大愤慨。大部分新闻由苏联俄罗斯的塔斯社（Tass News agency）提供。

该报无疑正在接受苏联政府的资金，并按照其指示行事。
日本审查当局已开始关注该报，如有必要可能会予以取缔。

In a letter to the Editor of the "Novosti Dnia" Max
ARSKY, who just has been released from gaol after serving 50
days imprisonment for larceny, gives way to his feeling of de-
pression and bitterness over lack of sympathy and understand-
ing displayed by the general public in connection with his case.
He maintains that he is prevented from earning his living by
working in his professional capacity, against which unfair and
callous attitude he protested by committing the larceny in
question. He also expresses his gratitude to the Editor of the
"Novosti Dnia" for the latter's impartial attitude towards his
case and for pointing out the nature of his protest.

The writer then proceeds with a violent outburst di-
rected against newspaper "Slovo" and its editor, a translation
of which reads as follows:-

" Your humane attitude towards me may be better under-
stood if compared with the attitude of the dumb "Slovo" which
kicked at me on that occasion with its ,fortunately unshod,
hoofs of a crippled old gelding.

This ,probably, came in a way of gratitude for that I
had saved this paper once from your accusations which, as I un-
derstand now, were fully justified.

At that time these tapsters rushed to me for help:
"Save us! We are perishing!"

And I saved them!

But then at least an educated person was at the head
of this "beauty". Now, however, it is run by a sluggard who can-
not even stand on his own feet and therefore remains seated not
even at the head, but literally on the head of this paper; like
fish, newspaper. This is why this paper stinks from its head,
as a fish does. It stinks very badly, it stinks because of its
own decomposition and because of the absurd position of the in-

马克斯·阿尔斯基（Max ARSKY）在致《今日新闻》编辑的一封信中发泄了他的抑郁和痛苦之情，他此前因盗窃罪服刑50天，刚获释。他对公众在其案件中表现出的缺乏同情和理解感到不满。他声称，他被阻止以其专业身份谋生，为了抗议这种不公平和冷漠的态度，他实施了上述盗窃行为。他还感谢《今日新闻》编辑对其案件持公正态度，并指出了其抗议的性质。

随后，作者对报纸《言论报》（Slovo）及其编辑进行了激烈的抨击，译文如下：-

“如果你将我的人道态度与哑巴《言论报》的态度相比，你会更好地理解我，那家报纸当时用它那‘幸好未穿鞋’的残废老骟马的马蹄踢了我。

这‘可能’是出于感激，因为我曾使这家报纸免于你们的指控，我现在明白，那些指控是完全正当的。

当时，这些酒保冲向我求助：
‘救救我们！我们要完蛋了！’

而我救了他们！

但至少那时，这个‘美人’是由一个受过教育的人领导的。然而现在，它由一个懒汉经营，他甚至无法站立，因此不是坐在头部，而是 literally 坐在这家报纸的头上；就像鱼一样，报纸。这就是为什么这家报纸像鱼一样从头开始发臭。臭气熏天，因为它自身的腐烂以及那个人的荒谬处境，

Письмо Макса Арского.

М. Г. г. Редактор.
Писать можно многое и о многом.
Но для чего и кому?
Если общественности, в строгомъ смыслѣ этого слова, нѣтъ, а слѣдовательно нѣтъ моральной опоры и поддержки, если человѣку на вопросъ — что ему остается дѣлать, раз ему запрещено заниматься его основной, обозначенной даже въ паспортѣ, профессіей артиста и журналиста, если, на вопросъ — что ему, кончать самоубійствомъ или бороться, онъ слышитъ непревосходимый по цинизму отвѣтъ: — "Дѣлайте, что хотите!"
Если все это никого, т. е. так наз. общественность, не возмущаетъ — для чего и кому писать?
Какой можно ожидать положительный результатъ и кого тронуть.
Потомъ, разв первый человѣкъ погибаетъ въ зыбучихъ пескахъ равнодушія если не бездушія.
Да еще на фонѣ такихъ великихъ потрясеній, когда гибнутъ безслѣдно тысячи, десятки — сотни тысячъ людей при самыхъ возмутительныхъ условіяхъ и обстоятельствахъ, при томъ безвинно, совершенно незаслуженно, вмѣсто группки небольшой, но лютой и вполн, казалось-бы, заслужившей уничтоженія.
В такой обстановк — какое можетъ имѣть значеніе судьба одного индивидуума для окаменѣвшихъ представителей человечества.
Потому и цѣль моего письма — исключительно поблагодарить васъ г. редакторъ, за ваше пониманіе моего отчаяннаго положенія, въ которое поставила меня оловячная фраза:
"Длайте, что хотите!"
Я человѣкъ дисциплинированный, и все что я дѣлаю, я дѣлаю только съ точки зрѣнія закона или, по крайней мѣрѣ, съ разрѣшенія тѣхъ, кто стоитъ на стражѣ закона, дѣлаю даже то, что не хочу, когда мнѣ говорятъ "дѣлайте, что хотите".
Я искренне благодарю васъ, г. редакторъ, за безпристрастное отношеніе вашей уважаемой газеты, отмѣтившей и подчеркнувшей на этомъ фактѣ мое безбрежныя факи и мародерство моего протеста.
Особенно явственно, Велико мнѣ человѣческое отношеніе, наряду съ тяжеловснымъ и безсловеснымъ "Словомъ", одновременно латнувшимъ меня, къ счастью неполновсными копытомъ искалченнаго мерина.
Вѣроятно въ благодарность за то, что въ свое время я спасъ эту газетину отъ варваровъ, теперь понялъ, совсѣмъ не справедливыхъ обличеній.
Тогда эти цѣловальники бросились ко мн за помощью: — выручай, погибаемъ!
И я выручилъ.
Но тогда во главѣ этой "прелести" стоялъ хоть человѣкъ съ образовательнымъ цензомъ.
А теперь — просто нецензурный ухарь, который даже не можетъ стоять, а потому сидитъ, и даже не во главѣ, а прямо на головѣ, безсловесной, какъ рыба, gazетины, отъ него воняетъ пыба и "пахнетъ с головы". Очень дурно пахнетъ. Пахнетъ и своимъ собственнымъ разложеніемъ и неисправимымъ положеніемъ субъекта, не только не обладающаго редакторскимъ цензомъ, но вообще судя по его "литератур" существомъ духовно и морально нецензурнымъ.
И вотъ когда я пришелъ къ нимъ на помощь, они сказали мнѣ: "Ступай вонъ, ты намъ не нуженъ, мы сами справимся". И я ушелъ.
Но слова изъ пѣсни не выкинешь...
Зато, теперь, какъ прегордо стоять на холмѣ въ одиночествѣ и чувствовать, что оно многолюдно.
Что же касается моей новой дѣятельности, то въ первое время, что-бы выглянуть прилично, мнѣ къ моему кофточкѣ остается пришить еще нижнюю юбку. Такимъ образомъ я буду одѣтъ, а остальное мнѣ дадутъ тѣ, кто щедро далъ мнѣ 50 коп.
Вотъ тогда "Слово" не посмѣетъ уже пѣть свою пѣсню, тѣмъ болѣе, что юбилейная статья, написанная мной, будетъ напечатана.

Максъ Арскій
4 сент. 1938 г.

马克斯·阿尔斯基的信。

尊敬的编辑先生。
可以写很多，关于很多事。
但为了什么，写给谁？
如果严格意义上的公众并不存在，因此也就没有道德支柱和支持，如果一个人被问到——既然他被禁止从事其主要的、甚至在护照上标明的艺术家和记者职业，他还能做什么，如果对于他是自杀还是斗争的问题，他听到的是无耻至极的回答：— “随你便！”
如果这一切都没有让任何人，即所谓的公众，感到愤慨——那么为了什么，写给谁？
能期待什么积极的结果，又能打动谁。
再者，难道第一个人不是消失在冷漠甚至无情的流沙中吗。
况且是在如此巨大的动荡背景下，成千上万、数十万人在最令人发指的条件下和情况下无辜地、完全不应地消失，而不是那一小群看似完全应该被消灭的凶恶之徒。
在这种环境下，一个个体的命运对于石化的人类代表来说能有什么意义。
因此，我写信的目的纯粹是为了感谢您，编辑先生，感谢您理解我被那句陈词滥调置于的绝望境地：
“随你便！”
我是一个守纪律的人，我所做的一切都是从法律的角度出发，或者至少是经过那些守护法律的人允许的，即使当有人对我说“随你便”时，我也会做我不愿意做的事。
我真诚地感谢您，编辑先生，感谢您尊敬的报纸对我的案件所持的公正态度，指出并强调了我无边无际的事实和我抗议的掠夺性质。
尤其明显的是，与沉重且无言的《言论报》相比，我的人道态度显得伟大，后者同时用不幸残缺的骟马的马蹄踢了我。
大概是为了报答我当时从野蛮人手中拯救了这份小报，现在我明白了，那些指控完全不公正。
当时这些酒保冲向我求助：— 救命，我们要完蛋了！
而我救了他们。
但当时领导这个“尤物”的至少是一个有教育资格的人。
而现在——只是一个粗俗无文的流氓，他甚至站不起来，所以坐着，而且不是坐在头部，而是直接坐在头上了，这份像鱼一样无声的小报，从他身上散发出鱼腥味和“从头臭起”。气味非常难闻。既散发着他自身腐烂的气味，也散发着那个主体不可救药的处境的气味，他不仅不具备编辑资格，而且总的来说，从他的“文学”来看，是一个在精神和道德上都不堪入目的存在。
当我去帮助他们时，他们对我说：“滚出去，我们不需要你，我们自己能行。”于是我走了。
但歌里的词是删不掉的...
相反，现在，骄傲地独自站在山丘上，却感觉周围人潮涌动。
至于我的新活动，起初，为了看起来体面，我除了我的小上衣外，还得缝上一条衬裙。这样我就穿戴整齐了，其余的将由那些慷慨地给了我50戈比的人提供。
到那时，《言论报》就不敢再唱它的调子了，更何况，我写的纪念文章将会刊登。

马克斯·阿尔斯基
1938年9月4日

Police Station,
Dear Sir,
We, the group of Russian Emigrants, are begging
you to pay some attention to the Russian Daily "Novosti
Dnia," edited by Chilikin. He from the name of the
Russian Emigrants is stating that we all are becoming
Soviets etc. This is an insolent lie. We want to live
peacefully and we shall never go over to the Bolsheviks.
Our children are not going to die in the country where
for the past twenty years Jews have been reigning.
Chilikin is a disgrace and a shame to Russians and we
are asking you to silence him. He and two brothers
Drozdoffs (one is a "journalist" another is employed
as a radio operator on the ship) are spies and
they have revolvers. It would be interesting to know
if they have a right to carry these revolvers.
Chilikin keeps his belongings at his home or in the
home of his lover - Greenhouse - ladies salon on
Dubling Well Road. She is a Jewess and a soviet
agent. They have connections with the Chinese
Communistic organizations and in the Soviet Consulate,
they can get finances as many as they want.

The leading article of the "Novosti Dnia," May 12,
1938 entitled "East of Suez" contains the following comment
on the suicides of Miss Viola Thompson and Mr. H. Hufner :-

"Hufner's letters as well as the investigations in-
to this matter have thrown a certain light on the circumstances
of this tragedy of two young persons.

According to Hufner's last letter, Viola Thompson,
his fiancee, died in the Country Hospital, "where no aid was
given her."

These last words in quotation marks sound rather
mysteriously, but the mystery will be cleared to a certain extent
if one recalls that Viola Thompson was, to use the Shanghai
expression, a "half cast," i.e. a half-breed, although this was
not very noticeable, as was the case of our great poet Pushkin.
Nevertheless, it was known in the town that there had been a
"coloured" person among Miss Viola Thompson's antecedents and,
it would seem, this fact was kept in mind.

Moreover, certain details have now become known which
show that behind Viola's suicide was the much talked about
racial "inferiority" for which, it would appear, neither the
brilliant abilities, nor industry, energy and attractiveness of
the girl could make up the mind of a European.

It is said that Hufner's parents in America knew about
his intended marriage. Shortly prior to his suicide Hufner, it
is believed, received a letter from them. In this letter his
parents expressed their views regarding his intended marriage.
It is said that they wrote him in the sense that, being of age,
he was free to marry any one he wished. At the same time they
hinted that, of course, he could neither expect their blessings
nor become a heir to their fortune; that should he come to
America together with his wife, he might come to their house, but

1938年5月12日《每日新闻》题为“苏伊士以东”的社论对维奥拉·汤普森小姐和H·胡夫纳先生的自杀事件发表了如下评论：-

“胡夫纳的信件以及对此事的调查，为这两位年轻人的悲剧情况提供了一定的线索。

根据胡夫纳的最后一封信，他的未婚妻维奥拉·汤普森死于乡村医院（Country Hospital），‘在那里她没有得到任何援助’。

这些加引号的最后几句话听起来相当神秘，但如果人们回忆起维奥拉·汤普森用上海的话来说是一名‘half cast’（混血儿），即半血统，尽管这一点并不十分明显，就像我们伟大的诗人普希金的情况一样，那么这种神秘感在一定程度上就会消除。尽管如此，镇上的人都知道，维奥拉·汤普森小姐的祖先中有一位‘有色人种’，而且，看来这一事实被人们记在心里。

此外，现在已知某些细节表明，在维奥拉自杀的背后，是人们热议的种族‘低劣性’，显然，无论这位女孩才华横溢、勤奋、充满活力且富有吸引力，都无法弥补欧洲人心中的这一缺憾。

据说胡夫纳在美国的父母知道他的婚约。据信，在自杀前不久，胡夫纳收到了他们的一封信。在这封信中，他的父母表达了对他拟议婚姻的看法。据说他们写信告诉他，既然他已成年，他可以自由娶任何他想娶的人。同时他们暗示，当然，他既不能指望得到他们的祝福，也不能成为他们财产的继承人；如果他带着妻子来到美国，他可以来他们家，但

she might not.
Rumours have it that on the eve of Viola's suicide,
Hufner let her know the contents of his parents' letter in such
an incautious manner, th~t it resulted in the suicide of the girl.
If all the above information is correct, one may say
that the circumstances which led to the suicides of Viola Thompson
and Henry Hufner are of a more deep nature and are more charac-
teristic of Shanghai than they might have appeared at the first
glance.
Where else, outside Shanghai, East and West, Europe and
Asia, the white and yellow races come into a closer contact?
Where else can be observed in the same degree the repulsion and
"struggle between various kinds of blood" instigated by doubtful
theories regarding the superiority of this or that kind of blood
....."
"Cases like the above expose the hidden emotions, under-
current sentiments which ferment in Shanghai. These undercurrent
emotions throw a somewhat different light on Shanghai which has
the reputation of an "international" city. To some people with
idealistic inclinations the word "international" usually implies
a peaceful and happy co-existence of all classes, peoples and
nations.
The case in question, the details of which we publish
as a rumour for what it is worth, shows that, apparently, the
latter conception of Shanghai is not quite correct. Somerset
Maugham, the Chehov of the modern English literature, calls it:
"East of Suez."

除了上海，还有哪里，东方与西方、欧洲与亚洲、白种人与黄种人会如此紧密地接触？
还有哪里能同样程度地观察到由关于某种血液优越性的可疑理论所煽动的对各种‘血液’之间的排斥和‘斗争’.....”
“像上述这样的案例暴露了在上海发酵的隐藏情绪和潜流情感。这些潜流情感为享有‘国际’城市声誉的上海投射出 somewhat different light（略有不同的光芒）。对于一些具有理想主义倾向的人来说，‘国际’一词通常意味着所有阶级、人民和民族的和平幸福共存。
本案的细节，我们作为谣言发布，其价值几何暂且不论，表明后者对上海的概念似乎并不完全正确。现代英国文学中的契诃夫——萨默塞特·毛姆，称之为：‘苏伊士以东’。”

Шанхай, 12 мая, 1938
EAST OF SUEZ...

В прошлом году в Шанхае с большим успехом прошел советский фильм «Цирк», в котором была удачно поставлена проблема расовой розни.
Между прочим, по ходу фильма неоднократно поется «Песня о Родине», ставшая популярной среди русских в Шанхае, и в ней есть, в частности, следующие строки:
— «Нет для нас ни черных, ни цветных».
Нам вспоминается этот фильм и эти слова в связи со следствием о самоубийстве Хафнера, бросившегося с крыши КСМП, после того, как отравилась его невеста.
Письма Хафнера и следствие пролили некоторый свет на обстановку и некоторые детали разыгравшейся трагедии молодых людей.
Согласно предсмертному письму Хафнера, его невеста, Виола Томпсон, скончалась в Мантри-госпитале, «где ей не было оказано никакой помощи».
Последние слова в кавычках звучат несколько загадочно, но загадка до известной степени расшифровывается, если припомнить, что Виола Томпсон была, как говорят в Шанхае, «half-cast», то есть полукровка, хотя и очень слабо выраженная, пожалуй, даже не мист, а самой публике был нам веленный тип Пурани.
И все-же в городе было известно, что в каком-то из ночных клубов рода Виола Томпсон была чем-то сценой, и это, конечно, не забывалось.
Кроме того, также были слышны некоторые слухи, относившиеся за то, что в некоторых кругах существовало предубеждение против смешанных браков.
Говорили, что у Хафнера были родители, которые не одобряли его выбора.
Что касается до Виолы Томпсон, то она, по слухам, имела связь с одним американцем, который обещал жениться на ней, но потом отказался.
По слухам, накануне самоубийства Виолы, Хафнер поделился с ней содержанием этого родительского письма, и настолько достоверно, что результатом был финал с ядом и смерть в госпитале.
Если все эти сведения точны, можно сказать, что самоубийство Виолы Томпсон и Генри Хафнера имеет более глубокие, специфически шанхайские корни, чем думалось первоначально.
Где, как не в Шанхае, более всего соприкасаются Восток и Запад, Европа и Азия, белая и желтая раса. Где, как не здесь, наряду с соприкосновением, живет место и первое отталкивание,—сборба кровей, поджигаемая всякими темными теориями о превосходстве той или иной крови.
Случай с Томпсон и Хафнером не единичен. Только на днях нам пришлось услышать, как один иностранец, живя с женщиной не одного с ним происхождения, заболел и лег в госпиталь. До его болезни жена пользовалась всеми благами и преимуществами его положения наравне с ним. После его отъезда в госпиталь, блага немедленно ушли от нея. Ей немедленно отказали во всех сторонах и правах, хотя она осталась жить в той же квартире, в той же обстановке, женой своего мужа. Кредиторы вскоре объявили себя ее врагами, и никто из прежних друзей не хотел иметь с ней никаких сношений.
Таким образом, случай с Томпсон и Хафнером является лишь одним из многих случаев, когда расовые предрассудки играют роковую роль в жизни людей.
В Шанхае, где встречаются представители всех рас и народов, особенно важно понимать и уважать друг друга, чтобы избежать подобных трагедий в будущем.

上海，1938年5月12日
苏伊士以东...

去年，一部苏联电影《马戏团》在上海大获成功，其中成功地提出了种族仇恨的问题。
顺便提一下，在电影进程中多次演唱了《祖国之歌》，这首歌在上海的俄国人中很流行，其中特别是以下几句歌词：
— “对我们来说，没有黑人，也没有有色人种”。
联想到哈夫纳（Hufner）自杀的调查，我们想起了这部电影和这些话，哈夫纳在其未婚妻中毒后，从工部局警察总局大楼屋顶跳下身亡。
哈夫纳的信件和调查为这场年轻人悲剧的环境和一些细节提供了一些线索。
根据哈夫纳的遗书，他的未婚妻维奥拉·汤普森死于曼特里医院（Mantri-hospital，音译，原文如此，前文为Country Hospital），‘在那里她没有得到任何帮助’。
加引号的最后几句话听起来有些神秘，但如果记得维奥拉·汤普森是上海人所说的‘half-cast’，即混血儿，虽然表现得很微弱，也许甚至不是穆拉托（mulatto，黑白混血），而是公众熟知的普兰尼（Purani，音译，可能指欧亚混血）类型，那么这个谜团在一定程度上就解开了。
尽管如此，城里的人都知道，在维奥拉·汤普森家族的某个夜总会背景中有一些事情，这当然没有被忘记。
此外，还听到一些谣言，认为在某些圈子里存在对异族通婚的偏见。
人们说，哈夫纳的父母不赞成他的选择。
至于维奥拉·汤普森，据传她与一名美国人有关联，该美国人曾承诺娶她，但后来拒绝了。
据传，在维奥拉自杀的前夕，哈夫纳与她分享了他父母来信的内容，而且非常确凿，结果是以服毒和在医院死亡告终。
如果所有这些消息都准确，可以说，维奥拉·汤普森和亨利·哈夫纳的自杀具有比最初认为的更深层、更具上海特色的根源。
除了上海，哪里还有东方与西方、欧洲与亚洲、白种人和黄种人最多的接触点。除了这里，在接触的同时，还存在着首要的排斥——血液的斗争，被各种关于某种血液优越性的黑暗理论所点燃。
汤普森和哈夫纳的案例并非孤例。就在几天前，我们不得不听到，一名外国人与一名非同一出身的女性同居，生病住进了医院。在他生病之前，他的妻子与他平等地享受着他地位带来的所有好处和优势。在他去医院后，这些好处立即离她而去。她被立即剥夺了各方面的权利，尽管她仍作为丈夫的妻子住在同一套公寓里，处于相同的环境中。债权人很快宣布自己是她的敌人，以前的朋友中没有人愿意与她有任何往来。
因此，汤普森和哈夫纳的案例只是众多案例中的一个，在这些案例中，种族偏见在人们的生活中起着致命的作用。
在上海，这里汇聚了所有种族和民族的代表，相互理解和尊重尤为重要，以避免未来发生类似的悲剧。

Translation from Russian newspaper "Novosti Dnya", May 7,
1938. Published by the Russian Publishing Co. 620 Avenue
Foch. Editor - Mr. V.M. Chilikin.

MISS V. THOMPSON'S UNTIMELY DEATH

Yesterday, after a short illness, the death took place
of Violet Thompson, a popular girl among the younger set of
Shanghai. She was the steno-typist of Mr. Pettit, the General
Secretary of Foreign Y.M.C.A.

Visitors calling on Mr. Pettit could not fail to notice
the charming girl with big black eyes and pleasant smile.

The death of Violet Thompson is a tragical happening.
Some days ago, she was suffering from tooth trouble and vi-
sited a dentist. Probably, the dentist was negligent as du-
ring the treatment an abscess was formed below the tooth, which
later caused the inflammation of the nerve and the weakness of
the heart's action, same leading the young girl to her grave.

The sudden death of Miss Thompson suggested at first
that she committed suicide. This was only brought forward
because her sister committed suicide about a year ago.

The elder Miss Thompson was also a pretty girl. The
reasons for her death were not explained, but it was supposed
that she did commit suicide because of an unfortunate love
affair.

Violet Thompson, however, had no reasons to commit sui-
cide. She had a good position; lately she was engaged to Mr.
□□□□, of the "Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury".

Her numerous friends in Shanghai and the family of Miss
Thompson deeply regret the untimely death of the unfortunate
young girl.
pages.zh:
译自俄文报纸《每日新闻》，1938年5月7日。由俄国出版公司出版，地址：福煦路620号。编辑：V.M. Chilikin（奇利金）先生。

V·汤普森小姐的早逝

昨天，经过短暂的疾病后，维奥莱特·汤普森去世，她是上海年轻一代中受欢迎的女孩。她是基督教青年会（Y.M.C.A.）外籍总干事佩蒂特（Pettit）先生的速记打字员。

拜访佩蒂特先生的访客无不注意到这位有着黑色大眼睛和迷人微笑的可爱女孩。

维奥莱特·汤普森之死是一场悲剧。几天前，她因牙齿问题去看牙医。也许牙医疏忽大意，因为在治疗过程中，牙齿下方形成了脓肿，随后导致神经发炎和心脏功能减弱，最终将这位年轻女孩送上了坟墓。

汤普森小姐的突然死亡起初让人怀疑她是自杀。之所以提出这种说法，仅仅是因为她的姐姐大约在一年前自杀身亡。

年长的汤普森小姐也是一位漂亮的女孩。她的死因未作解释，但据推测，她是因为不幸的爱情而自杀。

然而，维奥莱特·汤普森没有自杀的理由。她有一份好工作；最近她与《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）的□□□□先生订婚。

她在上海的众多朋友和汤普森小姐的家人对这位不幸年轻女孩的早逝深感悲痛。

NOVOSTI DNIA, May 7, 1938

Возвременная 7/5
смерть В. Томсон.

Вчера послѣ непродол-
жительной болѣзни сконча-
лась популярная въ кругахъ
шанхайской молодежи. Віо-
летта Томсон, занимавшая
должность стенографистки
и машинистки генеральнаго
секретаря ХСМЛ Петтита.
Посѣтители, приходившіе
по дѣламъ къ Петтит, не могли
не вспомнить очарователь-
ной чернокудрой дѣвушки,
съ большими черными гла-
зами и веселой улыбкой.
Смерть Віолы Томсон от-
носится къ разряду трагиче-
скихъ. Нѣсколько дней тому
назадъ у Віолы заболѣлъ зубъ
и она отправилась къ врачу.
Врачъ, впрочемъ, допустилъ
какую-то небрежность, т.
к. во время леченія подъ
зубомъ образовался абсцессъ,
въ результатѣ котораго по-
слѣдовало воспаленіе нерва
и затмъ лѣвое сердеч-
ное предсердіе, которыя
свели молодую дѣвушку въ
могилу.
Неожиданная смерть миссъ
Томсонъ вызвала первона-
чально подозрѣнія о томъ,
что она покончила съ собой.
Эти толки были вызваны
тѣмъ, что наканунѣ тому
назадъ покончила съ собой ея
сестра.
Старшая Томсонъ была
также красивой дѣвушкой.
Причины ея смерти выяс-
нены не были, но предпо-
лагалось, что она покон-
чила съ собой изъ-за несча-
стной любви.
У младшей Томсонъ однако
не было никакихъ причинъ
кончить съ собой. Она жила
весело и пользовалась извѣст-
ностью въ качествѣ свѣтской
дѣвушки. Послѣ Х...
...друзья
и знакомые Томсонъ
выразили глубокое
соболѣзнованіе по поводу
ея безвременной кончины.

Miss Violet Thompson's untimely death.

死亡 V. 汤姆森。

在上海青年圈子中颇受欢迎的

维奥莱特·汤普森小姐的早逝。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
Translation from Russian newspaper "NOVOSTI DNIA", January 19,
1938. Published by the Russian Publishing Company, 620 Avenue
Joffre. Editor - M. A. Chilikin. Date 27 / 1 / 38

REALLY HAPPENED

The "Evening Post" in its issue dated January 13
reported that a Japanese army truck proceeding at a high
rate of speed along Nanking Road knocked down a Chinese
pedestrian who was crossing the road, after which the truck
in question disappeared. The Chinese pedestrian was reported
to have died in hospital later on that day.

"Novosti Dnia" reprinted this report of the "Eve-
ning Post", but later found that it was entirely incorrect.

The true facts of the case are as follows:-

According to the statements of a policeman and
foreign witnesses, the Japanese military truck was proceeding
at a moderate rate of speed.

The Chinese pedestrian, when crossing the road,
passed behind a moving tramcar so that the driver of the
truck did not see him. As soon as he noticed the pedestrian,
he applied the brakes and swerved to the left in an attempt
to avoid the collision. However, the right front part of the
truck hit the pedestrian, causing serious injuries to his
head.

The driver stopped his truck immediately and as-
sisted a policeman to carry the injured person to the pave-
ment. The victim was then taken to a hospital where he was
later visited by members of the Japanese Military headquar-
ters accompanied by a doctor. They expressed their wish to
defray the costs of medical treatment of the victim.

（左侧手写批注：The Editor is responsible for this item. To inform Hong in connection with Evening News of & Every thing else in this paper may be very well handled but L is right from）

（印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 20. JAN. 1938 73）

译自俄文报纸《今日新闻》（NOVOSTI DNIA），1938年1月19日出版。由俄国出版公司出版，地址：霞飞路620号。编辑：M. A. Chilikin。日期 38年1月27日

确有其事

《字林西报晚刊》在1月13日的一期中报道说，一辆日本军用卡车沿南京路高速行驶，撞倒了一名正在过马路的中国行人，随后该卡车逃逸。据报道，这名中国行人于当天晚些时候在医院死亡。

《今日新闻》转载了《字林西报晚刊》的这篇报道，但后来发现该报道完全失实。

案件的真实情况如下：-

根据一名巡捕和外籍证人的陈述，那辆日本军用卡车当时以中等速度行驶。

那名中国行人在过马路时，从一辆行驶中的电车后方穿过，导致卡车司机未能看见他。司机一旦发现该行人，立即刹车并向左转向，试图避免碰撞。然而，卡车的右前部仍撞到了该行人，致其头部受重伤。

司机立即停车，并协助一名巡捕将伤者抬至人行道上。受害者随后被送往医院，日本军方总部成员在一名医生的陪同下前往医院探视。他们表示愿意承担受害者的医疗费用。

（左侧手写批注：本条消息由编辑负责。就《晚报》及本报其他所有内容通知洪先生，但L的观点是正确的）

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别科 1938年1月20日 73）

（左侧手写批注：已悉。Dali。1月20日。助理处长致副处长（特别科））

（底部手写签名及批注：1月20日。助理处长致副处长（特别科））

pages.en:
Как это было
на самом дѣлѣ.

13-го января «Ивнинг Пост» помѣстила замѣтку о том, что грузовик японской арміи, шедшій быстро по Нанкин роуд, сбил китайца, переходившаго дорогу и скрылся, китаец же из-за полученных раненій скончался въ госпиталѣ.

«Новости Дня», перепечатавъ эту замѣтку, потом узнали, что «Ивнинг Пост» от начала до конца дала неправильную информацию.

По полученным нами свѣдѣніям, инцидент произошел таким образом.

По показаніям полицейскаго и свидѣтелей - европейцев, военный японскій грузовик шел съ умѣренной скоростью.

Китаец, переходившій улицу, прошел сзади двигавшагося трамвайнаго вагона так, что шоффер грузовика его не видал, а когда он его замѣтил, то дал тормазъ и свернул влѣво, чтобы избѣжать несчастья, однако правое крыло грузовика зацѣпило прохожаго и он получил серьезныя поврежденія головы.

Грузовик послѣ этого остановился и шоффер помог полицейскому перенесть раненаго на тротуар. Затѣм китаец был перевезен въ госпиталь, гдѣ его посѣтили чины японскаго штаба съ доктором. Они осмотрѣли раненаго и выразили желаніе принять на свой счет всѣ расходы по лѣченію.
pages.zh:
实际情况如何。

1月13日，《字林西报晚刊》刊登了一则简讯，称一辆快速行驶在南京路上的日本军队卡车撞倒了一名过马路的中国人后逃逸，该中国人因伤势过重在医院死亡。

《今日新闻》转载了这则简讯，后来得知《字林西报晚刊》从头到尾提供了不实信息。

根据我们获得的消息，事件经过如下。

根据一名巡捕和外籍证人的证词，日本军用卡车当时以中等速度行驶。

过马路的那名中国人从一辆行驶中的电车后方穿过，致使卡车司机没有看到他；当司机发现他时，便踩下刹车并向左转弯，以避免发生事故，然而卡车的右侧翼子板刮蹭到了该行人，导致其头部严重受伤。

卡车随后停下，司机帮助巡捕将伤者抬到人行道上。之后，该中国人被送往医院，日本参谋本部官员偕同一名医生前往探视。他们检查了伤者，并表示愿意承担全部治疗费用。

In accordance with the instructions of the
D. C. (Special Branch), Mr. V.A. Chilikin, Editor of the
"Novosti Dnia" (Russian Daily News) was interviewed at head-
quarters on 29th December, 1937. He was informed that
his newspaper had come to the notice of the Japanese authorities
in connection with the important part it seemed to take in
anti-Japanese activities, and was warned to refrain from publish-
ing anything that might offend the susceptibilities of Japanese
nationals. He was given to understand that failure to comply
with this warning would result in the closure of his paper.

In reply Mr. Chilikin stated that since September 28,
1937, when the ban on his journal was lifted, no representations
had been made to him regarding any article appearing in the
"Novosti Dnia". However, he was cognizant of the situation and
would pay the strictest attention to the instructions of the
police.

CLOSING DOWN OF THE "NOVOSTI DNIA"

The newspaper "Novosti Dnia", 620 Avenue Foch, edited by
V.A. Chilikin was closed down by the Shanghai Municipal
Police yesterday.

At 3 p.m. a police party under Inspector U. Logan of the
Special (Political) Branch arrived to the offices of the
newspaper in a motor car. Mr. Logan produced to the em-
ployees of the newspaper who were present at the office,
an order for the closure of the NOVOSTI DNIA signed by the
Deputy Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police.
The printing offices of the newspaper were then closed and
a Chinese constable was left on the premises with the in-
structions to see that no work was carried out in the print-
ing department of the "Novosti Dnia". However, the offices of
the newspaper were not sealed.

asked regarding the reasons for the closing down of the
newspaper a representative of the Special Branch, S.M.P.,
stated that the "Novosti Dnia" had been closed down for
having systematically published articles likely to cause a
breach of peace and order and lead to undesirable inci-
dents, as well as for inciting one part of the population
against another, which cannot be tolerated at present when
events of such importance are taking place in Shanghai.

pages.en:
Draft

With reference to the contents of the undated petition
submitted to the Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal
Council by Mr. R.G. Allman on behalf of the Russian Daily News
(Novosti Dnia), I have to state that the newspaper in question
was established in March 1933 by Mr. V.A. Chilikin, and that its
present daily circulation is approximately 1500 copies, a figure
that does not agree with that mentioned in the first paragraph
of the petition.

In August 1935 following warnings from the French Police
to discontinue his blackmailing activities, Mr. Chilikin, the
editor and publisher of "Novosti Dnia," removed the editorial
and printing offices of his publication from the French Concess-
ion to the Settlement. This was followed in September of the
same year by the French Police placing a temporary ban on the
sale of the newspaper in the French Concession.

Since December 1936 until the present time, "Novosti
Dnia" has officially come to the notice of the Municipal Police
on no less than ten different occasions in connection with
either complaints lodged against the editor, or against
objectionable and untruthful articles published in the newspaper.
Warnings by the Police to refrain from continuing with articles
of this nature have remained unheeded, and it would appear that
Chilikin never intended to pay any attention to advice tendered
by the Police.

With the suspension of his newspaper by the Municipal
Police on September 8, Chilikin made no attempts to conceal his
anti-Police sentiments during the course of every day conversation,
and it was not until he realised the futility of endeavouring
to obtain 'protection' elsewhere for his newspaper against the
'persecutions' of the Municipal Police that he deemed it advis-
able to express his regrets and submit the present petition.

Past experience has shown that Chilikin has been entirely
indifferent to the good names, reputations and interests of
persons and institutions which he chose as the targets of his
slanderous attacks, whilst previous promises made by this
individual to cease his defamatory, libellous, offensive,
pages.zh:
草案

关于R.G.奥尔曼先生（Mr. R.G. Allman）代表《俄罗斯日报》（Novosti Dnia）向上海工部局总秘书提交的未注明日期的请愿书内容，本人谨声明，该报由V.A.奇利金先生（Mr. V.A. Chilikin）于1933年3月创办，其目前的日发行量约为1500份，这一数字与请愿书第一段中提到的数字不符。

1935年8月，在法国巡捕房警告其停止勒索活动后，《俄罗斯日报》的编辑兼出版人奇利金先生将其刊物的编辑部和印刷厂从法租界迁至公共租界。同年9月，法国巡捕房随即暂时禁止该报在法租界销售。

自1936年12月至今，《俄罗斯日报》因针对该编辑的投诉，或因该报刊登令人反感及不实文章，至少十次正式引起市警察局的注意。警方曾警告其停止刊登此类文章，但均未获理会，看来奇利金从未打算重视警方提出的建议。

随着其报纸于9月8日被市警察局停刊，奇利金在日常交谈中毫不掩饰其反警情绪，直到他意识到试图 elsewhere 为其报纸寻求“保护”以对抗市警察局的“迫害”是徒劳的之后，他才认为表达悔意并提交当前请愿书是明智之举。

过往经验表明，奇利金对他选择作为诽谤攻击目标的人物和机构的名誉、声誉及利益完全漠不关心，而此人此前作出的停止刊登诽谤、诋毁、冒犯性、

In view of these remarks, it would appear that the
brief period of suspension already imposed on "Novosti Dnia"
is not of sufficiently lengthy duration to impress upon its
editor the necessity for correctly treating the reputations
and interests of private persons and institutions, and for
keeping articles appearing in the publication within the
bounds of common decency.

鉴于上述情况，目前对《俄罗斯日报》实施的短暂停刊期似乎不足以让其编辑深刻认识到必须正确对待私人和机构的声誉与利益，并将刊物上刊登的文章控制在基本得体的范围内。

Dear Mr. Fessenden,

On behalf of the Russian Daily News, I herewith submit this petition to you, the Shanghai Municipal Council, and Chief Police, for permission to continue the publication of the above daily paper. This paper has been in circulation and publication for more than five years has a daily circulation in this community of more than 15.000 copies daily.

It employs many Chinese and other Nationals in its publication, and the paper is unable to continue to pay these employees' wages if permission is not granted to begin the publication.

The Editor and Publisher regrets if he has inflicted injury or caused the Police any trouble concerning this matter, he deeply regrets if he has caused injury to any parties or organization in the community caused by statements in his paper.

The Editor and Publisher states that he will exert every effort possible to see that any statements repulsive, offensive, or improper will not be published in the future, he is willing to give a guarantee satisfactory to the Police that he will in good faith try to conform to the above statements if permission is granted for him to continue to publish the paper.

Yours very truly,

I was a Russian the answer was "Yes". During the course of
the conversation which followed Chilikin expressed his
indignation over the closing of his newspaper and stated that
it had been closed owing to the influence of certain pro-
Japanese elements "It is the work of Inspector Smeianoff of

Tcheremshansky of the S.M.P. who are my personal enemies and
enemies of my newspaper. The newspaper was of a strictly
pro-Chinese Character and it appears that the pro-Japanese
elements are still strong in the Settlement. It remains to
be seen yet who wins in present hostilities, the above intrigue
may cost some people their heads. Now I am sending to Nanking
full information regarding the closure of the newspaper and

The Police allegations that they are doing me a favour is
nonsense. I hate to think of any fear of any group of Russians
planning to assault me. I hate any person or institution of
pro-Japanese character, because Japan is bound to lose as she

Translation from the "SHANGHAI ZARIA", September 9, 1937
9 9 37

CLOSING DOWN OF THE "NOVOSTI DNIA"

The newspaper "Novosti Dnia", 620 Avenue Foch, edited by
V.A. Chilikin was closed down by the Shanghai Municipal
Police yesterday.
At 3 p.m. a police party under Inspector W. Logan of the
Special (Political) Branch arrived to the offices of the
newspaper in a motor car. Mr. Logan produced to the em-
ployees of the newspaper who were present at the office,
an order for the closure of the 'NOVOSTI DNIA' signed by the
Deputy Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police.
The printing offices of the newspaper were then closed and
a Chinese constable was left on the premises with the in-
structions to see that no work was carried out in the print-
ing department of the "Novosti Dnia". However, the offices of
the newspaper were not sealed.
Asked regarding the reasons for the closing down of the
newspaper a representative of the Special Branch, S.M.P.,
stated that the "Novosti Dnia" had been closed down for
having systematically published articles likely to cause a
breach of peace and order and lead to undesirable □□ inci-
dents, as well as for inciting one part of the population
against another, which cannot be tolerated at present when
events of such importance are taking place in Shanghai.

译自1937年9月9日《上海柴拉报》（SHANGHAI ZARIA）
1937年9月9日

《NOVOSTI DNIA》停刊

由V.A.奇利金编辑的位于福煦路620号的《Novosti Dnia》报昨日被上海公共租界工部局警务处查封。
下午3点，由特务科（政治股）W.洛根督察（Inspector W. Logan）率领的一队警员乘车抵达该报办事处。洛根先生向在场的工作人员出示了一份由市警察局副警务处长签署的查封《NOVOSTI DNIA》的命令。随后，该报印刷厂被关闭，并留有一名华籍巡捕在原地，指令其确保《Novosti Dnia》印刷部门不进行任何工作。然而，该报办事处并未被封条封闭。
当被问及查封该报的原因时，市警察局特务科代表表示，《Novosti Dnia》因系统性地刊登可能破坏和平与秩序并导致不良 □□ 事件的文章，以及煽动一部分居民反对另一部分居民而被查封，在上海发生如此重大事件的当下，这种行为是不能容忍的。

归档
2BR
9月9日

这是一种非常令人厌恶的感觉
当你确知自己注定要灭亡
而当各国正在撤离时
你的命运却是维持和平与秩序。

加入志愿队，
戴上马刺和钢盔——哦，多么美丽！——
看着其他国家的妇女和儿童
匆忙离开这座城市。

荣耀归于英雄，归于培育了
这些英雄的俄罗斯传统。
只可惜无人关心
拯救我们的母亲、妻子和婴儿……

（印章：1937 年 9 月 7 日 上海 总办处收讫）

作为替代，我们得到了钢盔
并受到了非常客气的感谢。
我们在致报社的信中受到了赞扬。
至于我们的家人身处炮火之下这一事实……

（批注：Dr. Cumming）
（批注：DBBiga）
（批注：8-1 Rees）
（批注：Chase）

好吧，别在意那个——我们有 Metzler（梅茨勒）做我们的公使！
他会采取一切必要措施，
让全世界为之震惊，
让外滩因嫉妒而脸色发青……

他将从一位日本女性朋友那里包租所有舢板
送我们所有人“回祖国”……

当你确知
自己被视为一文不值时，
这是一种令人厌恶的感觉……
你比印度人还不如，
你有点像祖鲁人——
一个白皮肤的无用野蛮人！

（印章：1937 年 9 月 13 日 上海 总办处收讫）

pages.en:
-2-

Even for the Indians a reason was found
For their safe removal from the gaol,.
Only we emigrants are not even as good as criminals -
We are the only homeless ones here...

We are wandering amidst dead bodies,
And we are subsisting on soup
Which is given us in return
For our carrying rifles and bandoliers...

Well,the defence of peace and order
Is not a bad thing,
It is our sacred and unquestionable duty.

But,knowing our duties well,
We ask: "What about our rights?
Are words a sufficient compensation for any service,
Particularly for service such as this?"

While we are protecting the interests of other people,
Most noble,indeed,will be those nations
Who will consent to take our kiddies on board their ships...

But why should they worry
If a Russian company can be formed at a moment's notice?
Would it not be sheer waste of money
To evacuate their old men,wives and children?

It's a very nasty feeling
When you know for sure
That no one will afford you protection,
That no one is inclined to waste time and energy
On us - people of no importance...

Well then,lads, what are we going to do?
We whom the fates so cruelly persecute?
Shall we continue to refer to our life here as a struggle
While we await the opportunity to return to Russia?
pages.zh:
-2-

即使是印度人，也找到了理由
将他们安全地从监狱中撤出，
只有我们这些侨民甚至不如罪犯——
我们是这里唯一的无家可归者……

我们在尸体间徘徊，
靠喝汤维持生计，
这是对我们
携带步枪和子弹带的回报……

好吧，维护和平与秩序
并非坏事，
这是我们神圣且不容置疑的责任。

但是，既然我们深知自己的责任，
我们要问：“那我们的权利呢？
言语是否足以补偿任何服务，
尤其是像这样的服务？”

当我们保护他人利益时，
那些同意让我们的孩子登上他们船只的国家，
确实是最高尚的……

但他们何必担心
如果一家俄罗斯公司可以瞬间成立呢？
撤离他们的老人、妻子和孩子
岂不是纯粹浪费金钱？

当你确知
无人会为你提供保护，
无人愿意在我们这些
无足轻重的人身上浪费时间和精力时，
这是一种非常令人厌恶的感觉……

那么，伙计们，我们该怎么办？
我们这些被命运残酷迫害的人？
在等待返回俄罗斯的机会时，
我们要继续把在这里的生活称为斗争吗？

pages.en:
-3-
НЕПОКОЛЕБИМЫ И СКРЕПЕНЫ,
Shall we keep on thinking
That we are as firm as rocks,
And that there are no obstacles in our way?
And at the same time, being men,
Bend our spines before every foreigner?

To bend our spines before our own people,
Before the "moujiks" - oh, no! It's a shame!
Better to bow to a foreigner,
Better even to kiss the heels of the dogs
Who are living on islands!
Japan

women/
It's a nasty feeling when and children
are being segregated according to passports which they
possess,
And what do we care as to who was hit by the shells
and taken to hospitals.

We are here a second-rate people.
Then why, the devil, should we worry
About the first-rate people?

Let ships come and go
Taking these people with them
And clearing Shanghai of their presence...

We are accustomed to hardships,
And having acquired a good knowledge
Of the cultured nations
We are not complaining to them:
They are not likely to be moved by words,
Or by tears
Or even by the shedding of blood....
pages.zh:

НЕПОКОЛЕБИМЫ И СКРЕПЕНЫ, [坚不可摧且紧密团结，]
我们要继续认为
我们坚如磐石，
且前方没有障碍吗？
同时，身为男人，
却在每个外国人面前卑躬屈膝？

向我们的同胞，
向“穆吉克”（农民）卑躬屈膝——哦，不！那是耻辱！
最好向外国人鞠躬，
最好甚至去亲吻
生活在岛屿上的狗的脚后跟！
日本

妇女/
这是一种令人厌恶的感觉，当人们
根据所持护照
对儿童进行隔离时，
至于谁被炮弹击中并被送往医院，
我们毫不在乎。

我们这里是二等人。
那么，见鬼，我们何必
为头等人士操心？

让船只来来去去
带走这些人
并将上海从他们的存在中清理出去……

我们习惯了艰难困苦，
并且对文明国家
有了很好的了解
我们不向他们抱怨：
他们不太可能被言语打动，
或被眼泪打动，
甚至不会被流血打动……

August 21, 1937.

Kong Chan (抗戰), a three-day periodical, published the
following article on August 19 :-

LETTER FROM RUSSIAN DAILY NEWS TO MADAME SUN YAT-SEN

(Editor's note: The following is a letter sent
by the Russian Daily News (俄文每日新聞), a local newspaper
established by White Russians, to Madame Sun Yat-sen
expressing their sympathy with China's resistance. It will
be seen that the Japanese Imperialists are common enemies
of the world.)

"Madame Sun Yat-sen,
    "Please allow us to use the name of the Russian
Daily News to express our greatest sympathy at this time of
China's crisis.
    "We must now explain the rumour current in various
circles of China to the effect that White Russians living in
China are joining hands with the Japanese. This is completely
erroneous because the majority of White Russians living in
China, especially those residing in Shanghai, would never do
anything to harm China. We are preparing to join hands with
China and fight against the enemy of China and Russia.
    "For a long time the greatest enemy of Russia has
been Japan. Japan has sent spies to Russia and has continued
to cause trouble on the boundary of Russia. She oppresses
Russians and Chinese in 'Manchukuo'.
    "Although our paper has been in circulation for
many years, yet this is the first time that we have given a
sincere explanation to the Chinese people. We will not change
our attitude towards China and will continue to resist the
enemies of China and Russia.
    "Russian residents in Shanghai all sympathize with
China. Only a small number of shameless elements and news-
papers connected with 'Manchukuo' impair the friendly relations
between China and Russia.
    "Russia and China are both at present facing the
terror of fighting and foreign interference. This will only
strengthen the consolidation of the Russian people. We
believe that in the present critical situation, China will
become still more united.
    "Our unchangeable slogan is: 'China and Russia
are friendly to each other and will join and assist mutually
in the struggle against the Japanese Imperialists!

                        "The Russian Daily News,
                        "No.680 Avenue Foch,
                        "August 16."
